Synopsis:
Brazil's August IPCA inflation came in below expectations at 4.22% YoY (vs 4.27% forecast), with a monthly decline of -0.32% — the steepest drop since August 2022. Key drivers were temporary: one-off electricity discounts (Itaipu dam), lower airfares, fuel, and food prices. After four consecutive 25bps cuts bringing Selic to 14%, analysts at Capital Economics and Pantheon Macroeconomics expect another 25bps cut to 13.75% at the upcoming BCB meeting, though no acceleration in easing pace is anticipated given the temporary nature of the softness.
